<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

Reviewed at 8473217, together with whatwg/fetch#1755 at 958e7eb. The Fetch anchors this PR links to (`opaque-response-safelist-check`, `request-no-cors-media-request-state`, `request-no-cors-javascript-fallback-encoding`) exist in that PR, and the fallback encoding for classic scripts is set in the right place.

**Blockers**

- [Every later range request](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/8473217c2b96454422c08f7dcf99b30cf14bf9ee/source#L39388-L39391) is marked "subsequent" and [fetched from the media resource's URL](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/8473217c2b96454422c08f7dcf99b30cf14bf9ee/source#L39292-L39296), with redirects followed. Fetch's opaque-response-safelist check lets "subsequent" responses through without sniffing. So a media server can serve a real first range and then redirect a later range request to a cross-origin endpoint that ignores `Range` and returns 200 JSON or HTML, and ORB lets that response through.
  - The [explainer](https://github.com/annevk/orb#changes-to-requests-and-media-elements) has subsequent range requests use the URL of the initial response and not follow redirects.
  - [The note here](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/8473217c2b96454422c08f7dcf99b30cf14bf9ee/source#L39310-L39312) assumes the initial range was sniffed as audio or video, but nothing checks that.
  - Consider recording the URL of the initial response once it has been allowed, using that URL for subsequent requests, and only issuing them after that.
  - Not following redirects needs a change in Fetch, because main fetch rejects no-cors requests whose redirect mode isn't "follow". I raised that on whatwg/fetch#1755.

**Suggestions**

- *verify a media response* [links "extract content-range values" to Background Fetch](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/8473217c2b96454422c08f7dcf99b30cf14bf9ee/source#L2719). whatwg/fetch#1755 defines that term in Fetch, though it isn't exported yet. Once it is, consider pointing this link at Fetch.

</details>
